To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have generated and characterized new MAbs recognizing distinct FcRII receptor isoforms.

we have generated three monoclonal anti-human FcRII2b antibodies with different epitope specificities and have shown that the epitopes recognized by these antibodies are located within the extracellular domain of the receptor.
we have generated three MAbs that recognize different epitopes of the human FcRIIs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a set of new MAbs which are suitable tools to analyze the FcRIIs in vitro as well as in vivo.
the generation and characterization, using recombinant human receptors and synthetic peptides, of new monoclonals recognizing the human FcRIIA and FcRIIIB isoforms.
the generation and characterization as well as the application of new monoclonals antibodies that recognize distinct human FcγRII isoforms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antibodies described in this study are valuable tools to study the FcRIII isoform distribution on cells of the human immune system.
the MAbs ID2.7 and II8D2 can be used for the identification of the FcR gamma chain-associated isoforms FcRIIc1 and FcRIIi1.
the MAb II1A5 is a pan FcRIII MAb, the MAb ID2.7 a pan FcR II MAb and the MAb II-8D2 an anti-FcR IIb MAb.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we generated and characterized three MAbs that are useful for the detection of human FcRIIs at the protein level.
we generated three MAbs that can be used to discriminate between the various FcRII receptor isoforms.
the MAbs described here represent a powerful tool in the field of FcRII research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MAbs described in this study can be used to study the expression pattern of the Fc gamma receptors at the protein level.
we have generated three new MAbs that can be used to discriminate between the FcRIIA and FcRIIIB isoforms.
these new MAbs can be used to characterize the cell type distribution of FcRII on various immune cells.
